channel.title: Echoes of a Monster
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Echoes of a Monster" - "Given enough time, and with enough of us trying to look into this void, something crawled out of it."

item.title: Re: Echoes of a Monster
item.content:encoded:
Hey there, thanks for the crit!

+ Here are my Responses +
- Close -

This feels like although I think a pattern screamer does hate all existence… they don't seem like murderous beings, so much as wanting to erase existence as a concept?

This is a completely valid point here, but these are special circumstances. I'd liken it to this situation: you've been locked in a basement, and a person begins torturing you. Do you hate the person who locked you in the basement or the person torturing you more? I, personally, would hate the torturer more, as while being locked in a basement is bad, the torturer makes it much worse. Even though I'd hate the person who locked me in the basement for enabling the torture, I'd hate the torturer more for, well, torturing me.

In this case, our world is the 'basement' for this entity; it hates being here. However, the people actively perceiving it (and their brains 'filling in the gap' of the entity, trying to make it real) are the torturer/s, and thus it hates them more. It's not murderous per se, more 'defensive' (as I said in my response to cybersqyd, it's lashing out). And in this case, lashing out is all it can do. It can't get rid of the basement, so it gets rid of the torturers.

ALSO, I don't understand this concept of someone becoming a pattern screamer… which doesn't seem to fit at all. These things are unknowable, pure hatred machines that exist outside of reality.

Again, valid point. I, uh, didn't really explain what's happening here, so I'll do that now. In my headcanon for SCP-3930, when people enter the void they become a pattern screamer, quickly losing their minds as they come to terms with the fact that they don't exist, and can't, but are being made to exist. This entity essentially acts as a smaller version of the void, in that it drags people into itself so that they cease to exist (and thus, as part of my headcanon, become a pattern screamer). It also kind of warps everything around it slightly (space trying to fill in what should be a gap, but it isn't). Hope this makes sense!

[1]I just don't think this will add much to the concept. [2]And in terms of having an enjoyable horror story, I don't think this is innovative enough. [3]Again, I don't think that Pattern Screamers fits this sorta story format at all (horror comes out of something and hunts down people in a facility).

Let's sort this out in sections:
[1] - I disagree with you slightly here. Mostly because I myself am curious about the incident mentioned in the SCP-3930 article (also found in my summary: "Given enough time, and with enough of us trying to look into this void, something crawled out of it."), and this could serve as an explanation for a presumably terrifying incident that isn't elaborated on whatsoever. However, this is only assuming I could execute this successfully, which may happen, but might not.
[2] - I mean, I can't really argue with you here. More of a matter of taste really.
[3] - To reiterate, this is building off of a serious incident that is only vaguely mentioned in the source article. While this tale mightn't be a good fit for the Pattern Screamers ordinarily, due to extraordinary circumstances I believe it does fit as an elaboration on an incident.

Basically, this Tale aims to fill in a gap in the story of SCP-3930, whilst still maintaining the whole 'unfathomable unreality' feel that is so present within it.


Anyway, thanks again for the crit, hope this helps with your concerns!

item.title: Re: Echoes of a Monster
item.content:encoded:
Hey, thanks for the crit (and thanks for the greenlight)!

I'm just going to clarify some things, hopefully they clear up your concerns:

+ Open Clarification +
- Close -

I…think my biggest concern about this idea is that it feels too much like it's pulling back the curtain around pattern screamers to reveal that they're just generic murder monsters: this feels like it'd be stronger if everything was almost exactly as it is now except there's no entity.

Yeah, I really didn't have much description about this 'entity' I mentioned (despite the plot revolving almost entirely around it), so I'll clear it, and its motives, up now.

The entity itself is the non-existent manifestation (I know this is an oxymoron) of the very existent hatred of the non-existent pattern screamers. Its 'form' isn't actually seen in this tale, in fact, it doesn't really have a form (being non-existent). My best attempt at describing it is like a barely perceivable 'wrinkle' (our brain filling in the gap that is this entity to its best extent) in the space in front of us, or the reflection of an invisible being in a warped mirror.

Now for its motives. The entity, being the non-existent manifestation of very real hate, is simply a vessel for the pattern screamers' malice and rage against those who have given them existence. It kills not because it can, but because its very non-existent existence is torment, and, like the pattern screamers, it hates. Like a terrified wild animal that lashes out against the people trying to help it, it lashes out against the scientists trying to perceive it. Once there are only ten people aware again, the hate (from the pattern screamers) fuelling it loses its potency, and it proceeds to bolt back to where it came from (this is what I meant by it 'disappearing': its presence was no longer felt).

The thing is, this creature is intelligent. Like the pattern screamers who birthed it, it can communicate and understand language1 (in this case, Russian, like the soldiers who were sent into the void and never returned). Throughout the tale, I'll have it scrawl things like 'I'm scared', 'STOP LOOKING AT ME', and 'Why are you doing this to me?' into the walls and floors of the facility. This should really work to up the 'creep' factor of this tale, which I intend to have mainly consist of paranoia and psychological horror (e.g scientists looking into an empty room and not knowing whether the creature is there or not. Any deaths will be completely out of the blue).

And that's about it for my clarification. Thanks for reading, and I hope this clears some things up!

Footnotes
1. Evidence of this is in the exploration log, where a pattern screamer tells the D-Class to lean back. My theory is that the pattern screamers share a hive mind of information and knowledge from its victims, and this is how the entity can communicate and understand why it is suffering.

item.title: Re: Echoes of a Monster
item.content:encoded:
I…think my biggest concern about this idea is that it feels too much like it's pulling back the curtain around pattern screamers to reveal that they're just generic murder monsters: this feels like it'd be stronger if everything was almost exactly as it is now except there's no entity.

My other concern is that the plot feels very much like a generic sort of, horror/slasher film plot; where there's a monster gradually picking off the characters until only a few are left; and…I think it's not a huge deal here just because the actual progression is so bizarre and surreal; but I do think this means you're heavily relying on actually nailing doing indescribable horror well which can be really hard to do.

I'm…going to greenlight this though just because I do genuinely think this can work and that you have a good idea of how you're going to pull it off.

item.title: Re: The Monster that Didn't Exist
item.content:encoded:
Hey again, thanks for the recrit!

+ Open Response +
- Close -

[…]weird to see a Foundation observation site with no means of self-defense[…].

Again, this would be relevant to almost any other article, but this one is somewhat of an exception. The Site (at the time of this tale) is a ramshackle observation facility in the middle of nowhere set up by a couple of Soviet scientists to monitor and study a poorly understood anomaly (not GRU Division "P"). Due to only functioning as observation of a static anomaly which presents no immediate danger to its surrounds (unless one enters it), there would most likely to no weapons stored on-Site (lack of funding/unnecessary)1. Dr Vasiliev himself mentions that they tried sending in soldiers with recording equipment, but they didn't return.
However, even if there were weapons on-Site (and the scientists had basic combat training), they would understand that firing bullets at something that doesn't exist has as much of an effect as sneezing on it, or asking it politely to leave.
There'd probably be security, sure, but it would be far outside the Site to (as I mentioned in my footnote) prevent people from intruding.
I think that's how things would work, correct me if I'm wrong.

Anyway, thanks for the recrit, hope this clarifies some things!

Footnotes
1. Maybe a couple to prevent people from intruding, but even then the weapon supply would be minimal.

item.title: Re: The Monster that Didn't Exist
item.content:encoded:
NP. I just think that it would be weird to see a Foundation observation site with no means of self-defense, especially given that everyone working for The Foundation knows about the risks in serving it. It just feels weird that there isn't even security mentioned. Not to mention that basic combat training wouldn't be that hard to implement, even on a voluntary basis. And no one would even think to bring in something from home, like a taser or Airsoft pistol…?

The conversation would be interesting, so that would take out that problem. Sound great!

item.title: Re: The Monster that Didn't Exist
item.content:encoded:
Hey, thanks for the crit!

Here are my responses:
Wooooosh

1) Show at least two or three scientists getting weapons. If you really want to be fancy, show one getting to a weapons locker before getting killed, one getting a weapon before being killed, and the third shooting but missing before he's killed.

I don't… really know if this would work, purely for in-Universe reasons. This is an observation Site, nothing more, so it is unlikely that weapons are stored there. However, even if they were, these are scientists not trained for combat of any kind, so they most likely wouldn't know how to operate weapons in the first place. However (again), even if these scientists had combat training, they are up against an entity who is non-existence's hate made manifest (this monster, like the primary anomaly, doesn't exist), so the scientists would know that weapons, even anomalous ones, wouldn't work. This is why I believe this wouldn't work here. For almost any other article, this would be a great example of natural escalation, but here it just doesn't work logically.

2) The scream in his ear should increase in volume with each death. It should help your tension just a little more and add to the end.

This could work, I'll consider it. But I'll also consider that as the monster kills people, the pattern screamers would get less angry, not more, so I dunno if this would make sense.

3) Also, you need to have the "There can be only ten" come out somehow at least three ways before he gets it. Yeahyeah, I know I'm giving you lots of patterns to play with and I'm probably going over somehow. However, that's because patterns have strength, and I figure that hearing it just once just makes it a random message. Backing with a pattern makes it hard to ignore.

Again, I'll consider this. However, I was planning for Dr Vasiliev to have a conversation (admittedly, it would be mostly one-sided) with the voices (dead colleagues) in the static who explain what the rest of the pattern screamers want, before, like the rest, their voices degenerate into screaming howling and wailing. Might be contrived, but I like the idea of Dr Vasiliev's dead colleagues giving him an explanation with the last of their sanity.

Anyway, hopefully this clears some things up. Thanks for the crit!

item.title: The Monster that Didn't Exist
item.content:encoded:
A tale about SCP-3930, and what happened when something crawled out of it.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Standard (black highlighter theme to match SCP-3930's style)

Elevator Pitch: A tale of terror, paranoia, and suspense told from the terrified perspective of Dr Vasiliev as he desperately tries to figure out how to destroy this entity with minimal loss of life, all while distracted by a barely perceptible noise that is ringing in his ears.

+ Open Narrative +
- Close Narrative -

Central Narrative:
- Dr Vasiliev is monitoring SCP-39301 and notices a noise from the void, and something at its forefront. As he watches, the thing at its forefront drags itself out of the void and starts moving towards the Site
- Dr Vasiliev has just enough time to notify everyone on-Site that something is coming before it arrives
- The tale follows Dr Vasiliev as he runs and hides through the Site
- As he dismisses possible solutions, the tale's perspective switches between Dr Vasiliev (who is running and hiding) and various other scientists (who are running and are caught)
- When the scientists are caught, their perspective focuses on one of their five main senses and how the sense is distorted as they become a pattern screamer. Hearing is the only one not mentioned…
- Dr Vasiliev finds a radio and hears voices in the static that tell him there can be no more than ten, after which he tells everyone to gather in the cafeteria
- Dr Vasiliev counts 11 people and reluctantly notifies them that one of them has to die to stop the entity
- As they are having a discussion, the door where Dr Vasiliev and one other scientist are standing bursts open
- The perspective switches to the scientist next to Dr Vasilev as that scientist is attacked, focusing on hearing. However, the perspective switches back to Dr Vasiliev before things get weird
- As the scientist dies and the entity faces Dr Vasiliev, he realises the sound he's hearing is also coming from the entity
- The entity (and the sound) begins to slowly disappear, and as they do Dr Vasiliev realises what he's been hearing this whole time: the faintest, almost imperceptible sound of screaming

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The name of the article (and probably the article this tale is associated with) would draw the reader's attention, and the subject (scientists hunted by the unfathomable) would also hook the reader in.

Additional Notes: None

That's it for now. Thanks for reading, and hopefully this is intriguing!
P.S Sorry about that Zyn

Footnotes
1. It wasn't called that back then, but I'm still thinking of a name.
